Ford Motor Company. Ford believes that NHTSA's conclusion on sulphate emissions is incorrect. Rather, Ford believes that no increase in such emissions will result from planned MY 1979 catalyst changes, at least as far as Ford NPA's are concerned.
Ford stated that it appears that the EIS conclusion on increased sulphate emissions is pased on the assumption that such emissions are proportional to the amount of noble metal used in catalysts, which is not the case. They stated that published data indicate that oxygen content of the exhaust gas stream is of major importance in sulphate formation, and catalytic converter size or the amount of catalyst (noble metal) is not a factor.
Summary. GM, EPA and Ford state that sulphate emissions will not increase in MY 1979.
Analysis. The EIS is corrected to reflect these comments which basically state that anticipated increases in sulphate emissions related to increased size of catalytic converters required to meet the fuel economy standard for MY 1979 were overestimated. NHTSA incorrectly assumed that sulphate emissions were proportional to catalyst proportions rather than to the amount of excess oxygen in the exhaust stream.
